title: Evaluation of BCC for psychologically distressed heart patients in the psychosomatic outpatient department at the University Medicine Göttingen, Germany
summary:
PsyCordiAmus is a project to determine whether holistic, patient-centered support based on the Blended Collaborative Care (BCC) approach is feasible in our psychosomatic outpatient clinic and whether this improves the well-being of patients.
In our psychosomatic outpatient clinic, we support patients with heart disease and psychological disstress. For this support, trained treatment assistants (care managers, CM) work with the patient's treating doctor/s under the supervision of a team of clinical specialists in the outpatient clinic. For the first time, this is taking place under routine conditions in a university psychosomatic outpatient clinic in Germany. With the PsyCordiAmus study, we will evaluate how well this is going and how helpful it is for our patients.
conditions: Combination of mental distress annd chronic heart disease

interventions.name: We will include 50 psychologically distressed patients with heart disease, who receive a treatment offer in the sense of Blended Collaborative Care in our psychosomatic university outpatient clinic, into the longitudinal observational study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
2. Diagnosed chronic heart disease (e.g. heart failure, CHD, arrythmias)
3. Mental distress (HADS > 12 and/ or diagnosed mental disorder according to ICD-10) 
4. Participation in blended collaborative care programm in the psychosomatic outpatient clinic of the University Medicine Göttingen (UMG)
Exclusion criteria:
no consent to participate in the study
